headline: 5 Common Mistakes People Make After a Drug Arrest

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
When you're facing a drug charge, it's natural to feel panicked, but certain actions can unintentionally make your situation much worse. Avoid these common missteps to protect your future.

1. Talking to Law Enforcement Without a Lawyer: Anything you say can be used against you. Politely but firmly state that you wish to have your attorney present before answering any questions.
2. Resisting Arrest: Even if you believe the arrest is unlawful, resisting can lead to additional, more serious charges. Cooperate physically, but invoke your right to remain silent.
3. Delaying Legal Consultation: Time is crucial. Evidence can disappear, and opportunities for defense strategies can be missed. Contact an attorney like Angelo J. Reyes as soon as possible.
4. Not Understanding Your Charges: Drug laws are complex, and penalties vary widely. Don't assume you know the full scope of what you're facing; let a legal expert explain it to you.
5. Discussing Your Case on Social Media: Anything you post online can be found and used by prosecutors. Keep details of your case private, even from friends and family, to avoid compromising your defense. Remember, your future depends on making smart choices during this challenging time.
